name: Bartimaeus
overview: Bartimaeus is a male blind beggar who is found outside in Jericho, as recorded in Mark 10:46. There is no mention of his tribe or additional personal notes. His condition and location uniquely identify him in the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Bartimaeus appears once in Scripture, specifically in Mark 10:46. No special meaning or divine origin is attributed to this proper name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Bartimaeus is explicitly identified as the son of Timaeus in Mark 10:46. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further details about his family or other relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Bartimaeus is significant in the biblical account as a blind man who calls out to Jesus for mercy while positioned outside Jericho. His story highlights themes of faith and healing, demonstrating the power of Christ to restore sight and transform lives. This encounter underscores Jesus' compassion and authority, central to the Gospel message.
